p: Distribution-fitted stacking and auto-stretch for PixInsight. NukeX stacks the FITS light frames you add (with optional flats): it fits a statistical distribution to every pixel's samples across the stack, estimates the signal from the fitted model, and applies one of its stretches (Auto is recommended). A camera quantum-efficiency (QE) database built into the module routes each frame and decomposes dual-narrowband colour data (HaO3 / S2O3) into emission lines. It loads on any Linux with glibc 2.34 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Rocky/RHEL 9+).

Network: one kind of connection only, the camera-database update check. It makes HTTPS requests to raw.githubusercontent.com (this repository), automatically at most once every 7 days when you open the NukeX window, and whenever you press Check now; it sends no identifier, usage data or image data. A newer database is downloaded and installed only if you agree, after its Ed25519 signatures are verified. Automatic checks can be turned off in the NukeX window. NukeX launches no external program. Files outside the PixInsight installation: ~/.config/nukex4/ (update-check state, a downloaded database, filter names you teach it, your stretch ratings), a frame cache in ~/.cache/nukex4/cache/ while a run lasts, and progress files in /tmp. Documentation, including every network connection, external program and file location: doc/tools/NukeX/NukeX.html.
